knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a method for predicting protein contact maps using ESM-1b language model outputs and residual neural networks. It demonstrates significant F1-score improvements over single-sequence and evolutionary-profile-based predictors on independent test sets. The method addresses the computational intensity and data limitations of traditional evolutionary profile generation.

attributes.description: A contact-map predictor utilizing ESM-1b output, a large training set, and an ensemble of residual neural networks
attributes.advantage: Faster and reasonably accurate alternative to evolution-based methods for large-scale prediction

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the limitation of single-sequence contact map predictors by incorporating unsupervised features from the ESM-1b language model. It demonstrates that combining ESM-1b attention maps with one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs improves prediction accuracy for proteins with few homologs. The method was validated using a curated dataset derived from ProteinNet and independent test sets.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study defines three independent test sets: SPOT-2018, Neff1-2018, and CASP14-FM, to evaluate protein contact map predictors on sequentially isolated and homolog-free proteins. Input features for the neural network ensemble include one-hot encoding, SPOT-1D-Single outputs, and ESM-1b attention maps, with specific preprocessing applied to the attention maps. Performance is evaluated using standard CASP contact definitions and metrics such as F1-score, MCC, and AUC across short, medium, and long-range contacts.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study details the architecture of a 12-block ResNet model used for protein contact map prediction, utilizing specific hyperparameters and loss functions. It describes an ensemble of six models trained on different feature combinations, including ESM-1b attention maps and one-hot encodings. The method is compared against other predictors like SSCpred and TrRosetta, with a focus on feature importance and training strategies.

attributes.inspiration: ResNet architecture in protein contact-map and RNA secondary structure prediction

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates feature combinations for protein contact map prediction, finding that ESM-1b attention maps significantly outperform one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs. An ensemble of six models using direct and distogram-based strategies achieved higher F1-scores than individual models. On proteins without homologs, the proposed method outperforms evolutionary-based predictors and ESM-1b.

attributes.description: Ensemble of six models using direct and distogram-based contact prediction

knowledge_units.context_summary: SPOT-Contact-Single outperforms profile-based predictors and SSCpred on low-homology proteins, achieving higher F1-scores and significantly faster inference times. The method utilizes ESM-1b attention maps and an ensemble of ResNet architectures to predict contact maps without evolutionary information.

attributes.input_features: ESM-1b attention maps, one-hot encoding, SPOT-1D-Single output
attributes.length_limitation: cannot directly predict contact maps for proteins with more than 1024 amino acids
